introduction: Today, in the middle of Lent, the Church celebrates the solemnity of Saint Joseph, husband of the Blessed Virgin Mary and patron of the universal Church. The readings recall God's promise to David of a lasting house and kingdom, and Abraham, who believed against all hope. In the Gospel, Joseph, a righteous man, listens to the angel and takes Mary into his home. Let us ask Saint Joseph to teach us his quiet faith.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God entrusted his Son and the Virgin Mary to the care of Saint Joseph. With confidence, let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the universal Church, entrusted to the protection of Saint Joseph: that she may care for the Body of Christ with his faithfulness and tenderness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For fathers and for all who have the care of children: that they may protect and guide them with patience and love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For workers, for the unemployed and for all who struggle to provide for their families: that they may find dignified work and a just wage. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the dying: that, like Saint Joseph, they may go to God with Jesus and Mary beside them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may listen to God's word in silence and do what he asks of us, as Joseph did. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you chose Saint Joseph to be the guardian of your Son and the husband of the Virgin Mary. By his prayers, help us to trust you as he did and to serve you faithfully. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: A righteous man
reflection.body:
Saint Joseph never says a word in the Gospels. Yet the Church honors him with a solemnity in the middle of Lent, names him patron of the universal Church, and has always turned to him with great confidence. In 2020 Pope Francis wrote a whole letter about him, Patris corde, describing him as a father with a heart full of love.

The first reading looks back to the promise God made through the prophet Nathan: a son of David would reign forever. "I will be his father, and he will be my son." And again: "Your house and your kingdom will be made sure forever before you." Joseph is the link in that chain. Matthew calls him "Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus," and the angel greets him as "Joseph, son of David." Through him, Jesus belongs to the house of David.

The Gospel shows us what kind of man he was. When he learns that Mary is with child, Matthew says: "Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly." His righteousness is not harsh. It is just and merciful at the same time. Then the angel speaks to him in a dream: "Joseph, son of David, don't be afraid to take to yourself Mary as your wife." Joseph wakes and "did as the angel of the Lord commanded him." No argument, no delay.

Paul says of Abraham: "Against hope, Abraham in hope believed." The same could be said of Joseph. He did not understand everything, but he trusted God and acted.

Many of us live with plans that have been overturned, as Joseph's were. Today, ask his help in one concrete situation where you need to trust God without seeing the whole picture. And thank God for the people who, like Joseph, have quietly protected and cared for you.
